title: Forming a band; Bricktop's Grand Duc and Gene Bullard
summary: After Sissle left, Briggs formed a band for Sayag and describes Ada 'Bricktop' Smith, her marriage to Pete du Conge, and how she took over Gene Bullard's Grand Duc.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, so now you got left at --
Noble Sissle went back in the fall of 1930,
Yes.
Briggs
And then you --
Yes.
And around this time you began to get mixed up with the Hot Club? Is that right?
Yes, yes.
Well, that's very interesting. I'd like you to tell us about that.
Well, I reformed an orchestra. When Noble Sissle went back to the United States, I was asked to form an orchestra, by Mr. Sayag, the same man we worked for, for Ciro's.
Ciro's in Paris?
Yes, the same, yes.
And I formed the orchestra, and meanwhile there was a very fine person from Chicago, who was in Paris, and she had, what you would call a bar, that we called the Grand Duc. Ada Smith.
Briggs
Right.
Ada Smith, who became Madame du Conge, Bricktop du Conge.
She was married to t du Conge?
Yes. She had lived with us. Bricktop was Pete's wife.
Oh, is that right, I didn't know that.
They married in Paris. He met her in Paris. She was running that Grand Duc Cabaret.
That was her club?

Her club. If you ever walk down Rue Pigalle, before you get there, Rue Fontaine, there's a little cabaret, I don't know whether the name is still Le Grand Duc, on the lefthand side before -- you have another side street, Rue de Rouchefocourt.
Right.
End of Cassette 3, Side 1.
Briggs
We were talking about the location of the Grand Duc, which was Bricktop's place in Pigalle.
And this was just on the Rue Fontane, was it?
Yes, it was between Rue Fontaine and Rue Pigalle.
Oh, I see. Right.
That was her first club, when she first came, and that -- she came to Paris to work for a very famous man, who was a -- you've probably heard of him, who was a member of the Lafayette --
Escadrille.
Escadrille. Gene Bullard.
Gene Bullard, yes, I have heard of him.
Gene Bullard, and she came to work for him, 'cause he was the managing director of the Grand Duc at the time.
Briggs 238
And she was so successful, that, whatever happened I don't know, but Gene, he finally caved out, 'cause he had a gymnasium as well.
I see.
And I believe he had incurred certain debts and everything else, and that forced him to abandon the cabaret.
Well, whatever happened, she continued alone, and she did well.
